scope: Proposition 6.6 (Localization in an intermediate shell) of the manuscript “Self-dual random-cluster interfaces below one” (preprints/Self-dual-random-cluster-interfaces-below-one-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 223 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 bf15a86507a10184), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 71-72. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. statement: Let Qn be disks of Convention 6.1, with end arcs In, Jn and flanks Sn, Tn. Write ϱn for sup-norm radius about a tile-coordinate center, and suppose In ⊂ {ϱn ≤ rn}, Jn ⊂ {ϱn ≥ Rn}, 1 + rn = o(mn), mn = o(Rn), where mn is an integer. Put Sn(mn) = {3mn/4 < ϱn < 5mn/4}. After passage to a subsequence one of the following alternatives holds, with constants a > 0 and A < ∞ fixed on that subsequence. 71 (i) There is a proper Sn–Tn tile-edge crosscut of at most A edges in the safe shell Sn(mn). Its incident cells contain a physical bond route of either prescribed color between eligible flank slots, after moving each contact at most A tile steps within its own fan. In this case put ℓn = 1. (ii) There are scales ℓn → ∞, with ℓn ≤ Amn, and interior tangent disks of radii in [aℓn, Aℓn] touching the respective flanks. Their centers are joined by a simple polygonal route of length at most Aℓn, with an ordinary buffer of width at least aℓn away from its terminal approaches. At either contact, every wall portion accessible from the approach in a fixed contact neighborhood has that flank’s label and ordinary incident bonds up to its slots, and continues physically out of a larger contact neighborhood. The neighborhood radii and all buffer widths are fixed positive multiples of ℓn; all named geometry lies in Sn(mn). More precisely, with η = 10−3 there is a proper crosscut Kn of diameter ℓn such that no proper Sn–Tn crosscut of diameter less than ηℓn meets Nηℓn (Kn). The tangent disks can have radius ρn = ηℓn/100, with centers on Kn, and their contact neighborhoods are contained in this excluded neighborhood. This geometry satisfies the hypotheses of Lemma 6.4 in the companion pure law, including the planar caps on clear bulk buffers. Both statements hold in the split disk, also when the two accesses end at the same physical position through different incidences.
